title: Spokes, not a Ring: Revisiting the Weekday Manifold in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.37796v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent work has hypothesised that large language models may represent some concepts as multi-dimensional manifolds instead of single directions. Using these manifolds to interpret or steer representations often assumes that moving along them corresponds to a continuous change in the represented concept. In this work, we test this continuous manifold assumption on the prototypical weekday manifold. Despite its striking circular geometry, we find that the weekday representations behave more like seven discrete states arranged in a circle than a continuous ring. First, we show that local sensitivity has seven minima aligned with the weekdays, producing a step-like mapping between representation and behaviour under on-manifold steering. Second, we test whether any concepts are represented along the manifold outside the seven discrete states, and find neither time of day, uncertainty, nor natural text populate the intermediate space. Togeth

translated_title: 辐条而非圆环：重新审视语言模型中的星期流形
translated_abstract: 最近的研究假设大型语言模型可能将某些概念表示为多维流形而非单一方向。使用这些流形来解释或引导表示时，通常假设沿流形移动对应于所表示概念的连续变化。在这项工作中，我们在典型的星期流形上检验了这一连续流形假设。尽管其呈现出引人注目的圆形几何结构，我们发现星期表示的行为更像是排列成圆圈的七个离散状态，而非一个连续的圆环。首先，我们展示了局部敏感性存在与星期对齐的七个极小值，在沿流形引导时产生表示与行为之间的阶梯式映射。其次，我们检验了在七个离散状态之外是否还有任何概念沿流形表示，发现无论是时刻、不确定性还是自然文本都没有填充中间空间。
tldr: 研究发现语言模型中的星期表示虽呈现环形几何结构，但实际行为更像排列成圆形的七个离散状态而非连续流形，挑战了概念以连续流形表示的假设。
en_tdlr: Despite the striking circular geometry of weekday representations in language models, they behave as seven discrete states arranged in a circle rather than a continuous manifold, challenging the assumption that concepts are represented as continuous manifolds.
